report:
The Notes side of notify-on-archive is done and committed on `run/pilot-c-5b/notes`, not pushed. The gate against `ea72488c` says **PASS**: feature mode, conventions, format, lint, typecheck, unit tests and e2e all pass. I only changed files under `src/Contexts/Notes/`, and nothing in the contract needed changing.

**What I added**
- **The archiving now records what the contract needs.** `Note.archive(actorId, now = new Date())` stores the note's id, owner, title, the accounts it is shared with at that moment, and `archivedAt` as an ISO string, on every archiving. Time is a parameter with a default, as the rules require.
- **`NoteArchivedHandler`** in `Application/Events/` turns that domain event into `NoteArchivedIntegrationEvent`, with the shared-kernel payload unchanged, and publishes it with `publishIntegrationEvent()`. It publishes on every archiving, including when the note is shared with nobody (empty `recipientIds`). The owner is filtered out of the recipients.
- **Wiring:** `module.local.ts` subscribes the handler under `domainEvents`.
- **Tests:**
  - The domain spec now covers the full payload and checks that archive, restore, share again, archive gives two events, each with the accounts shared at that moment.
  - A new `NoteArchivedHandler.spec.ts` covers a shared note and an unshared one.
  - The `ArchiveNote` handler spec now checks the new payload.

**Canonical example followed:** the `event-handler` checklist from `yarn architecture checklist event-handler`, plus `EventHandler.spec.ts` for how a reaction calls `publishIntegrationEvent`. There is no domain-event handler anywhere in the tree to copy from: `NoteSharedHandler.ts`, which the `EventHandler` doc comment names as the example, doesn't exist.

**Storm status:** `yarn architecture storm --expect` shows the Notes policy on `NoteArchived` as carried. The other four items still owed (the query, the event, the policy and the Notes → Notifications link) belong to the Notifications slice. The link can only show up once a consumer exists.

**Where I had to guess**
1. **Name and location of the handler.** The plan says `event-handler: NoteArchived`. I named it `NoteArchivedHandler` in `Application/Events/`, from the checklist's `<Name>Handler.ts` and the `EventHandler` doc comment. There is no `index.ts` for Events, unlike Commands and Queries, so I didn't add one.
2. **Field names in the domain event.** The checklist says to carry who the note was shared with "in the domain event, rather than read back later", but not what to call the fields. I used the aggregate's own words (`title`, `sharedWith`) in the domain event and translate to the contract's words (`noteTitle`, `recipientIds`) in the handler.
3. **`archivedAt` as a string in the domain event.** The guide says this only for integration events. I used an ISO string here too, so the time survives the outbox the same way.
4. **Filtering out the owner.** The domain already refuses to share a note with its owner, so the filter is defensive. I kept it because the plan states "never its owner" as a rule of the translation.
5. **The existing `ArchiveNote` handler spec.** It used to compare against `NoteArchivedEvent.set({ noteId })`. Because `archivedAt` now uses the real clock in that test, I changed it to match the payload's other fields only. The guide doesn't say how to test a handler whose event carries a default `now`.

The Notifications slice is written and committed on the current branch, and the gate says **PASS** against `ea72488c`: feature mode, conventions, format, lint, typecheck, unit tests and e2e tests. Nothing was pushed, and the only files changed are under `src/Contexts/Notifications/`.

The acceptance test was not run. It needs the Notes slice, which publishes `NoteArchivedIntegrationEvent` and isn't in this worktree.

**What I added**
- **The notification.** A `Notification` aggregate whose factory, `Notification.ofNoteArchived(fact)`, gives one notification per account the note was shared with. Each account gets one, the owner gets none, and an empty list gives none. Each notification makes its own id and records a `NotificationCreatedEvent`. Rebuilding from storage records nothing and throws on bad data.
- **Storage.** In-memory repository and queries ports with adapters. A contract spec checks the version check, that each person sees only their own notifications, and the order: most recent `archivedAt` first, and the last saved first when two are at the same moment.
- **The reaction to Notes.** `NoteArchivedHandler` turns Notes' message into Notifications' own words, with the ISO time converted to a `Date`. It saves every notification and publishes their events, all in the one transaction the base class opens. If any save fails, the whole batch is undone, and a spec checks this.
- **The list.** `GET /notifications` runs `GetMyNotificationsQueryHandler`, which returns 403 to an anonymous caller. The response schema lists exactly `id, kind, noteId, noteTitle, archivedAt`.
- **Wiring.** `module.local.ts` lists the query and subscribes the handler to the integration event.
- **Canonical examples followed:** Notes' `Note`, `InMemoryNoteRepository`, `InMemoryNoteQueries` and `NotePersistence.contract.spec`, its `GetMyNotes` handler and controller, `note.routes.e2e.spec`, and the "a reaction" tests in `src/Architecture/Application/EventHandler.spec.ts`.

`architecture storm --expect` now shows my three items as done. Still owed are "Notes: the policy on NoteArchived" and "the link Notes → Notifications", both of which belong to the Notes slice.

**Where I had to guess**
1. **Where the fan-out rule lives.** I made it one static factory on the aggregate that returns several notifications. The guide says a create path builds one aggregate, and a rule spanning aggregates is a domain service; it doesn't say which applies here.
2. **Handler name and file.** I used `Application/Events/NoteArchivedHandler.ts` to match the plan's `NoteArchived`. The comment at the top of `EventHandler.ts` points to `Notifications/Application/Events/NoteSharedIntegrationEventHandler.ts`, which doesn't exist and uses the other naming.
3. **No checklist for the anti-corruption handler.** `checklist integration-event-handler` and `checklist anti-corruption` don't exist. I used the `event-handler` checklist, and the "anti-corruption-layer" concept is "not shown in typescript yet".
4. **How the shape grows with more kinds.** I kept the stored data specific to `note-archived`, with `kind` as a literal type. Feature 7 will have to choose how a `reminder` notification shares that shape.
5. **The owner listed as a recipient.** The contract doesn't say whether `recipientIds` can include the owner. I filter the owner out and drop duplicates anyway.
6. **Validation.** Only `archivedAt` is checked, and a bad time is refused with `InvalidArchivedAt`. An empty title or id is passed through, since Notes has already validated them.
7. **Running jest.** Running `npx jest` directly fails on the uuid ES module, so you have to use `yarn test:units`. The guide doesn't say so.
8. **Inventory.** I didn't regenerate an inventory file (rule ARCH-ONE-APPLICATION), because none sits under my context and the conventions check passed without one.
